quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #9
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 22

questions.question: When a car with bright headlights drives toward you at night, what should you do?

options.text: Stop until the other driver passes.
Look below their headlights.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at oncoming headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of the road until the other car passes. This prevents you from being blinded.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT safe on the interstate?

options.text: Slower traffic stays in the right lane.
Change lanes without signaling.
If you miss your exit, go to the next one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes without signaling.
questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes. Keep right if you are driving slower than other traffic. Never back up or make a U-turn on the interstate. If you miss your exit, go to the next one.

questions.question: When you have a green light and there are pedestrians in the intersection, what should you do?

options.text: You must yield to pedestrians.
You have the right-of-way over pedestrians.
Pedestrians must wait for you to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, you must yield to pedestrians in the intersection. Drivers must also yield to pedestrians when turning on a green signal.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Road construction or maintenance area.
Side road.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road construction or maintenance area.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn of hazards. Orange means construction or maintenance work ahead.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line in the center of a road mean?

options.text: A construction zone is ahead.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means any driver may pass when there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.
Slow-moving vehicle.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.
questions.explanation: This sign marks parking spaces for vehicles with disability license plates, disabled veteran plates, or disability placards.

questions.question: Which statement about alcohol and driving is true?

options.text: If you can walk in a straight line after drinking, it is safe to drive.
If you are under the legal alcohol limit, your driving is not impaired.
Alcohol affects judgment, which you need to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol affects judgment, which you need to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Alcohol hurts your judgment. You need good judgment to react safely while driving. Even small amounts of alcohol can affect your ability to drive safely, even if you are below the legal limit.

questions.question: If you are driving next to a single broken white line on the highway, what can you do?

options.text: You cannot cross the line to pass.
You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
You may only cross to change lanes if you are in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
questions.explanation: White broken lines separate traffic going the same direction. You may cross a broken white line to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: What is the purpose of rumble strips?

options.text: They alert drivers to tire problems.
They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.
They alert drowsy drivers with vibration and sound when their vehicle leaves the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They alert drowsy drivers with vibration and sound when their vehicle leaves the road.
questions.explanation: Rumble strips create noise and vibration to warn inattentive or drowsy drivers that they are leaving the road or approaching a stop sign or signal.

questions.question: When driving behind another vehicle at night, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your headlights on low beam.
Use high beam headlights until you are within 10 feet of the car ahead.
Use your high beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlights on low beam.
questions.explanation: Use high beams only in rural areas when no other cars are nearby. Switch to low beams when driving behind another vehicle.

questions.question: Should you drive on the shoulder to pass a car?

options.text: Yes, if the vehicle ahead is turning left.
No, never.
Yes, if the shoulder is wide enough.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: Never pass another vehicle on the shoulder. The other driver will not expect you there and may pull onto the road.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Watch for people crossing your path.
No passing zone.
Work zone ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: This orange sign warns drivers that roadwork is coming. Stay alert for temporary traffic control devices in the work zone.

questions.question: Sudden wind gusts on highways:

options.text: Generally affect only large vehicles.
Only cause visibility problems.
Can cause problems for all vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause problems for all vehicles.
questions.explanation: Strong wind can affect all drivers. Wind can reduce visibility by blowing dirt and dust, and it can physically move any vehicle.

questions.question: Use your headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days:

options.text: To keep your engine warm.
So others can see your vehicle.
To warn others of bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: So others can see your vehicle.
questions.explanation: In rainy, snowy, or foggy conditions, other drivers need to see your vehicle. Headlights make your vehicle more visible. If you turn on your wipers, turn on your low beam headlights too.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Reduce your speed when the pavement is wet.
The road ahead has many turns or curves.
More traffic is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed when the pavement is wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns drivers that the road is slippery when wet and they should slow down.

questions.question: Should you always drive more slowly than other traffic?

options.text: No, driving too slowly can block traffic.
Yes, it is a good defensive driving technique.
Yes, it is always safer than driving faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, driving too slowly can block traffic.
questions.explanation: Drive slowly in heavy traffic or bad weather. However, if you drive too slowly and block traffic flow, you can get a ticket.

questions.question: If a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle:

options.text: Beep your horn.
Expect the child to fully control the bicycle.
Expect the unexpected.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect the unexpected.
questions.explanation: Children on bicycles can be unpredictable. Young riders may suddenly change direction. Remember that children and bicycles are small and hard to see.

questions.question: When you approach an intersection with a flashing yellow light:

options.text: Stop before crossing.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Wait for a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, look for cross traffic, and continue carefully.

questions.question: If you face a green light but traffic blocks the intersection, you should:

options.text: Turn left and find another route.
Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.
Follow other vehicles into the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.
questions.explanation: Do not enter the intersection if traffic blocks your way, even with a green light. If the light changes while you are in the intersection, you will block cross traffic and may get a ticket.

questions.question: A steady red arrow on a traffic light means:

options.text: You cannot turn in that direction.
You can turn in that direction after a complete stop.
You can turn in that direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn in that direction.
questions.explanation: A steady red arrow means you cannot turn in that direction. Stop and wait for a green signal.

questions.question: You must always stop before crossing railroad tracks when:

options.text: There is not enough space on the other side for your vehicle to completely clear the tracks.
The railroad crossing is in a city or town with frequent train traffic.
You are carrying two or more young children in your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is not enough space on the other side for your vehicle to completely clear the tracks.
questions.explanation: A train can come on any track at any time, going in either direction. Do not start crossing unless you have room to completely clear the tracks before stopping.

questions.question: "BAC" means:

options.text: Blood alcohol concentration.
Big alcohol content.
Blood alcohol conservation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Blood alcohol concentration.
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures how much alcohol is in a person's blood. Drivers age 21 or older are considered to be driving under the influence when their BAC is 0.08 percent or higher.

questions.question: Extra space in front of a large truck is needed for:

options.text: Other drivers to merge onto the freeway.
The truck driver to stop the vehicle.
Other drivers who want to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck driver to stop the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more distance to stop than cars traveling at the same speed. Do not pull in front of a truck and then slow down or stop.

questions.question: Alcohol is:

options.text: A stimulant.
An antihistamine.
A depressant.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It weakens your judgment and makes your reflexes slow and unreliable.

questions.question: Alcohol in any amount is:

options.text: A stimulant.
A depressant.
Neither of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol in any amount is a depressant. It slows your nerve impulses and bodily functions. This reduces your inhibitions and hurts your ability to concentrate and stay alert.
